item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russia continues sabotage and missile attacks inside Ukraine, including a ballistic strike on Kyiv that killed one civilian and injured fourteen, and a fire near a weapons factory attributed to a Russia-run network. Ukrainian forces are carrying out deep-strike missions up to 2,500 km, hitting a missile-battery plant in Yelets and a chemical plant in Voronezh, and are evacuating wounded soldiers by drone. A US-brokered ceasefire is in effect in the occupied city of Oleshky, while European states pledge additional air-defence support. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Saudi-led coalition forces have responded by destroying Houthi missile tunnels, launchers and storage sites in Yemen and by striking additional missile facilities. Iran, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have agreed to hold more talks as the attacks continue. item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iran has intensified rhetoric, claiming the United States is not serious about talks, while the United States warned Baghdad it will strike Iraqi militias that join Iran's war. Iraq closed the Iran border crossing, sparking protests and turning the Al-Sheeb crossing into a contested corridor, and security forces raided the home of the Maysan provincial council chief for defying the closure. PKK-linked Yazidi militia units are disarming and joining the Iraqi army, and three militia groups have agreed to disarm by June 2027. Oil exports have returned to pre-war levels and a vessel caught fire off the Al-Faw coast. The conflict produced 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
Violent clashes continue across South Sudan, with government forces and SPLA-IO fighting in Wij-Panyikang, Upper Nile, and communal violence in Tonj North killing dozens. The government reported a 72‑person death toll in Tonj North, while victims of the Akol Koor residence clash are seeking over $340,000 in compensation from the Defence Ministry. Riek Machar denied commanding the White Army in court, and the South Sudan Bar Association launched a roadmap to improve access to justice. Canada emphasized media freedom as essential for peace, and the government and UN set a 2026 resettlement target after assisting 28,000 people since January. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

Over 35,000 people have fled the fighting across the border into Moyale, Kenya, prompting condemnation from regional leaders. item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:

Al Shabaab detonated an IED in Mandera, injuring six civilians, and Somali intelligence killed a senior al Shabaab operative. Heavy fighting erupted near Baidoa and in Burijeed as Laftagareen forces attacked army positions, prompting UN calls to halt the fighting amid famine, displacement and flood risks.
